newsitem.title: UK: EMU criteria more key than dates-Buba's Jochimsen.
newsitem.headline: EMU criteria more key than dates-Buba's Jochimsen.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen on Wednesday said the criteria for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) were more important than starting dates.
Jochimsen, in London for a conference, also said he would "wholeheartedly" welcome Britain's entry into a single currency at the start date.
The current scheduled start date for a single currency is January 1, 1999.
But Jochimsen said he saw signs of social unrest in France and other European countries due to the accelerated government efforts towards integration.

"I think the criteria are more important than dates," he said, adding that if politicians thought otherwise then the number of countries able to participate in the euro currency at first would be smaller.

Asked whether he favoured Britain being one of the founder members of a single currency, Jochimsen said: "I would welcome British entry into all integration efforts right from the beginning, wholeheartedly."
